steps.b:
Valence (valenca) is the number of bonds an atom forms — how many “hands” it has. Learn these by heart:

IH, Na, K, Ag, Cu, Cl (with metals)
IIO, Mg, Ca, Zn, Ba, Cu, Fe, S (with metals and H)
IIIAl, Fe, N (with H)
IVC, Si, S
VN, P
VIS

Some elements have several valences, shown in the name with Roman numerals: iron(II), iron(III).

Write the valences above the symbols and cross them as indices, then reduce:

AlIII OII → Al₂O₃
CIV OII → C₂O₄ → CO₂

Groups of atoms that stay together (polyatomic ions) work the same way and go in brackets when you need more than one: OH⁻ (I), NO₃⁻ (I), SO₄²⁻ (II), CO₃²⁻ (II), PO₄³⁻ (III), NH₄⁺ (I).

CaII (OH)I → Ca(OH)₂

An index (indeks) counts atoms inside one formula unit; a coefficient (koeficijent) in front counts whole units.

  • Ca(OH)₂: 1 Ca, 2 O, 2 H.
  • 3H₂O: 3 molecules → 6 H and 3 O.

steps.q: Write the formula of aluminium sulfate and count its atoms.
s: Al is III, SO₄ is II.

steps.e: Fe III, O II → Fe₂O₃ — the mineral hematite.

steps.q: How many oxygen atoms are in 2Ca(NO₃)₂?
steps.e: One unit has 2·3 = 6 O; two units have 12.
3 O × II = 6, so S is VI.
NH₄ is I, SO₄ is II → (NH₄)₂SO₄.
